tags.gist: Clarifies that dataset documentation makes validity, contamination and representativeness inspectable but does not establish any of them.
Suggests separating how well a device performs from what the evaluation asset was, so documentation can be machine-checked without being mistaken for a safety judgment.
Says judging contamination and representativeness needs documented provenance, population, annotation process, processing, partitions, quality records and dataset version.
Cites the commenter's own preprint finding that four public imaging datasets met only a fifth to two-fifths of evaluated documentation dimensions.
Recommends that construct-validity evidence come with structured, machine-checkable records describing the benchmark dataset itself.
Suggests, as an external standard, a machine-checkable minimum documentation layer for evaluation datasets, separate from any judgment of quality or performance.
Describes the commenter's open imaging dataset standard, its required provenance and version fields, and a validator that checks presence and structure only.
Offers the standard as proof the concept is implementable, recommending the concept rather than the standard itself.
Says a shared documentation layer would let third parties describe sequestered datasets without disclosing them and is an early candidate for standards work.
Says re-benchmarking against a premarket baseline needs the benchmark's exact version, subjects and partitions identified so asset changes do not confound device comparisons.
Notes subgroup analysis needs documented dataset composition, which a subject registry partly supplies, though not the dialect and literacy dimensions of R.2.
Suggests an origin declaration distinguishing acquired, synthetic, simulated, phantom-derived and mixed data, with generation methods recorded.
Notes the training-data provenance content of master files raises a similar documentation question that could use structured treatment.
Concludes with three recommendations: documented benchmark datasets beside validity evidence, a standardized documentation layer with versioning, and an origin declaration.
